The statute described in the provided text outlines the core requirements for valid consent under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Legally, this means that consent cannot be assumed through silence, pre-ticked boxes, or inactivity. Instead, it must be an active, affirmative action by the individual. The consent must be "freely given," meaning there is no significant imbalance of power or coercion; "specific," meaning it applies to a clearly defined purpose rather than vague blanket permissions; "informed," meaning the individual understands what they are agreeing to; and "unambiguous," meaning the intent to agree is clear and explicit. For businesses, this imposes a strict compliance burden to design data collection processes that capture and document this explicit consent, ensuring they can prove that individuals knowingly agreed to the processing of their personal data. Failure to meet these standards can result in significant regulatory fines and legal liability.
